title: Career Roadmap — Assistant Director
summary: An Assistant Director (AD) helps the director execute a production efficiently by coordinating cast, crew, locations, schedules and on-set activities. The role focuses on production planning, communication, timing and logistics.

blocks.text: An Assistant Director (AD) helps the director execute a production efficiently by coordinating cast, crew, locations, schedules and on-set activities. The role focuses on production planning, communication, timing and logistics.
Key responsibilities include script breakdowns, shooting schedules, call sheets, continuity coordination, rehearsals, crew communication and resolving production delays.

rows.text: Film language, screenplay analysis, communication and production basics

Shooting schedules, call sheets, continuity and shot planning

On-set coordination, rehearsals, location logistics and internships

Advanced scheduling, production management, networking and portfolio development
Complete a short film with documented AD responsibilities

blocks.text: For a three-year degree, combine the final milestones and prioritise practical set experience.

Practical experience is generally more important than collecting certificates. No single certification is universally required for Assistant Director roles.

Titles and hierarchy vary by production and industry. Becoming a director is a separate career path, not an automatic promotion from Assistant Director.
Explore FTII, SRFTI and Whistling Woods International. Verify current admissions, entrance requirements and fees.
A postgraduate degree is optional for many AD positions; hands-on experience and professional relationships can be alternative entry routes.
Potential destinations include the USA, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. Relevant programmes include film production, directing, production management and screen media.
Verify tuition, scholarships, work authorisation and production-placement opportunities before applying. An international qualification does not guarantee employment.

blocks.label: Primary recommendation
blocks.text: Prioritise practical film-set experience, script breakdowns, shooting schedules and call sheets. These demonstrate the organisational and communication skills needed to enter the profession.
